articles.summary: The Kansas Jayhawks won the recruiting battle for No. 1 overall recruit Tyran Stokes, and Stokes has looked the part early in his freshman season. There’s a...
articles.body:
The Kansas Jayhawks won the recruiting battle for No. 1 overall recruit Tyran Stokes, and Stokes has looked the part early in his freshman season.

There's a problem now, though, because Stokes has an injury, and it's going to require further examination.

Kansas is surely hoping to avoid a repeat of the odd Darryn Peterson injury saga of a year ago. Ideally, the Jayhawks can identify what's wrong with Stokes, treat it and get him back on the floor when he's ready.

There's still more information to come, though, and in the meantime, Kansas fans will hold their collective breath.

Stokes was hurt Tuesday night, and after the game, Kansas head coach Bill Self said that Stokes would be getting an MRI.

He sustained a lower-leg injury in the second half while battling for a rebound.

"It's a lower leg deal that he lost strength in his leg, and that's why he sat down, so I don't know anything more than that," Self said, via KUSports.com . "So MRI will probably tell us what the issue is. Didn't look bad to me, but sometimes things that don't look bad can be more serious than things that actually do look bad, so I'll reserve comment on seriousness because we have no idea yet."

Kansas was in the midst of a 102-77 win over UNLV at the Players Era 8 in Las Vegas, but Stokes' injury changed the feel of the night.

Stokes had played just 13 minutes before getting hurt, but he already had 13 points and 10 rebounds.

The MRI results should tell Kansas more, and the Jayhawks play again Wednesday night, so Self may have an update after the game.

Self pointed to a handful of players who stepped up in Stokes' absence.

He was a fan of the defense played by Keanu Dawes, and he also liked the offensive contributions of Leroy Blyden Jr., Taylen Kinney and Tre White.

"You know, Tre's one of those guys, as you guys have seen, he takes eight shots and gets 15," Self said. "He's just been very efficient for us, goes unnoticed a lot."

Kansas won't want to spend a long time without Stokes, but a bit of an absence will allow the Jayhawks' other contributors to find their rhythms and potentially make the team better in the long run — assuming it's not too bad an injury for Stokes.

articles.title: Dylan Larkin Standoff Puts Quinn Hughes’ Future in Minnesota at Risk
articles.summary: Dylan Larkin has made it clear he wants to play in Minnesota, and the Wild badly need another center. But Detroit holds the leverage, with Larkin under team...
articles.body:
Dylan Larkin has made it clear he wants to play in Minnesota, and the Wild badly need another center. But Detroit holds the leverage, with Larkin under team control for five more seasons. Recent reports suggest they're also being spiteful, refusing to trade him to his preferred destination. If the Red Wings dig in and say no, the effects could reach well beyond one trade.

The Athletic's Michael Russo said, "I really think that if they get Larkin, Quinn signs, like, the next day," though he called it "total conjecture." Hughes and Larkin skate together in the offseason and share an agent, and Hughes has said he'd take Larkin "in two seconds."

Admittedly, Hughes has also reportedly said a Larkin trade wouldn't automatically mean he signs. He also suggested that not getting Larkin would stop him from signing an extension.

All of this is to say that a trade isn't a guaranteed fix, but its absence removes one of the Wild's most compelling selling points.

Hughes is set to become an unrestricted free agent next summer. The speculation has long been that he wants to play with his brothers Jack and Luke in New Jersey, and the Devils reportedly have around $32 million in cap space in 2027-28. If Minnesota can't bring in someone he's really close with, why would anyone assume he'd stay? So far, winning doesn't seem to be what's motivating him.

Minnesota acquired Hughes from Vancouver last season, and losing him for nothing in free agency would turn a major gamble into a costly miss. The Wild would also be left without a top center and without their top defenseman.

A Hughes departure would free up significant cap space, which could push the Wild toward a major free-agent splash. It would mean a total pivot as the team tries to build around Kirill Kaprizov.

This is clearly the year for the Wild to go all in. Adding another solid player makes them arguably the NHL's Stanley Cup favorite, and if they're going to lose Hughes, GM Bill Guerin needs to stack the deck as much as possible before then.

Refusing a deal also costs the Red Wings. They don't look like a well-run organization, and if the Wild want to get Larkin out of there, it might be time to hammer home that narrative.

Larkin asked out last spring. He's yet to be moved. Simon Edvinsson is unhappy, ready to play back in Sweden if he's not signed by December 1. Detroit's asking price for both players is reportedly unreasonable, whereas the Wild have offered what many would consider a fair return. Rival executives are reportedly calling the Red Wings' asking price unrealistic.

Detroit has the right to wait for the right offer. And, while everyone believes Detroit is being spiteful, this could be a calculated bluff to get the Wild to up their offer. Minnesota has a lot to lose if they don't make this deal and that includes potentially losing a franchise defenseman.

articles.title: Baltimore mayor fires back at Ravens' Marlon Humphrey after controversial 'criminals' comment
articles.summary: Ravens CB Marlon Humphrey apologized for a critical comment about Baltimore, but the city's mayor is still hitting back.
articles.body:
Ravens CB Marlon Humphrey has taken polarizing stances over the years, including an appearance with U.S. president Donald Trump, but a comment about the city of Baltimore he made on his podcast is drawing backlash.

Humphrey's remarks even drew a response from Baltimore mayor Brandon Scott, who took a thinly veiled shot at the longtime Ravens cornerback in a statement.

Here's a look at what Humphrey said and how Scott is responding.

Humphrey drew backlash for saying Baltimore is "best at making criminals" during an episode of his podcast.

"What is Baltimore best at making?" Humphrey said, repeating the question out loud, before answering, "They're best at making criminals."

Humphrey has since deleted the podcast episode, but the comment predictably went viral.

Speaking to The Athletic , Humphrey apologized on Wednesday.

"As you guys know, I've been here my whole career. Spent lots of offseasons here, welcomed a son here. I'm an investor in the city, an investor in different areas [and] parts of the state," Humphrey said. "Obviously, I do know the effect that words have, and just would like to apologize for those comments."

The 30-year-old has spent a decade in Baltimore, earning four Pro Bowl selections with the Ravens and landing a First-Team All-Pro selection as recently as 2024. Humphrey regressed in 2025, however, and he could be on borrowed time with the franchise regardless of any off-the-field headlines.

Here's what you need to know about the response from the mayor of Baltimore.

Baltimore mayor responds to Marlon Humphrey

Baltimore mayor Brandon Scott acknowledged Humphrey's apology on Wednesday but said it is "not enough."

"Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper," Johnson said.

Johnson also took an apparent shot at Humphrey's play on the field.

"I wonder how he would feel if prominent Baltimoreans used their platforms to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way," Scott said, adding that no one would do that "because our team and city are supposed to be united as one."

Scott invited Humphrey to sit down with him and have a discussion with "some Baltimoreans who have re-entered our community."

articles.title: Heat’s Giannis Antetokounmpo ‘excited’ for Vice City night before GTA 6 release
articles.summary: MIAMI – With the Miami Heat excelling recently, with Giannis Antetokounmpo leading the way, Wednesday’s matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks is filled with s...
articles.body:
MIAMI – With the Miami Heat excelling recently, with Giannis Antetokounmpo leading the way, Wednesday's matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks is filled with storylines up the wazoo. As the sports world wonders how Heat captain and former teammate Tyler Herro will be after their physical altercation over the Summer and Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis Jr. facing their former team in the Bucks, the game also celebrates the release of "Grand Theft Auto VI."

13 years after the fifth installment in the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise, the sixth takes place in the fictional state of "Leonida," which is the video game's version of Florida, within the city of "Vice City," their version of Miami. The team and video game developer Rockstar Games have collaborated to bring the video game to life, such as releasing jerseys with the fictional city and even a new court with references to the game.

While Antetokounmpo wants to "keep the main thing the main thing," he understands the "hype" around the video game.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I understand the hype and feel like a lot of people in this room have played the game. They're excited for the game to come up. Just to be part of one of the most talked-about video games. It's fun. I heard that we have special jerseys and a special court, so I'm excited for that. I'm excited for the energy, but most importantly, meat and potatoes," Antetokounmpo said.

"Like, keep the main thing the main thing, the main thing is for us to come out here and win the game," Antetokounmpo continued. "You know, I hope the fans enjoy the energy; I hope there's fun things to do around the arena and outside the arena. I heard there's gonna be like cool cars and stuff. Probably my kids will go out there to take pictures with it. But daddy, me, myself, gotta do my job. You know, my job is to show up and try to win the game."

Heat's Erik Spoelstra interested in Grand Theft Auto VI

Various Heat players posted to their social media pages that Rockstar Games sent them a custom PlayStation 5 console with the game to celebrate the partnership, but someone who would want one is head coach Erik Spoelstra.

Besides talking about the night celebrating the video game, Spoelstra speaks on the storylines surrounding Antetokounmpo and Portis. Plus, Spoelstra sends "love" to the former Miami players coming to town, such as Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware, and Kasparas Jakucionis.

"That's the discipline. I mean, first of all, this is a really unique night. I think it's gonna be a lot of fun. It's going to be a global game tonight because of the setup with GTA. I think it'sawesome. I think it's fun. It's 10x everything, and to have that opportunity in a regular season game, I think, is exciting. I've never played the game before, but obviously I'm fully aware of it. If they want to send me a console, I'll play. I'm curious now. I want to play, and hopefully that will be its own distraction that we can put in that kind of box," Spoelstra said.

"Because I understand there's other emotions of our players, Giannis and Bobby coming over from over there, and there's a lot of history that they've had over there, so I know it means a lot to them," Spoelstra continued. "And then the four guys that we sent over there, a lot of emotions for them and for us. There's a human side to it. I know you know some of the storylines that are probably out there, but we really do view those guys in such a great regard. It is love."

At any rate, Wednesday night's game will be memorable for a lot of reasons, whether it's activities on and off the basketball court.

articles.title: 49ers’ Keenan Allen gets ‘savant’ label from former Kyle Shanahan WR
articles.summary: Keenan Allen may be new to the San Francisco 49ers, but his experience and route-running ability could make him an important piece of Kyle Shanahan’s offense...
articles.body:
Keenan Allen may be new to the San Francisco 49ers , but his experience and route-running ability could make him an important piece of Kyle Shanahan 's offense.

Former NFL wide receiver Andrew Hawkins had plenty of praise for Allen during an appearance on ESPN, calling the veteran receiver a "true savant" when discussing his ability to create separation.

" Keenan Allen is just as good at route running, and beating man-to-man, and separation. A true savant. He also understands zone," Hawkins said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Hawkins also explained why Allen's experience could be especially valuable in San Francisco. Learning Shanahan's offense is not an easy process, and it can take time for receivers to understand the system and develop chemistry within it. Hawkins acknowledged that even he needed time to get comfortable with the offense.

Allen, however, has the experience to make that transition easier . His understanding of route concepts and defensive coverage allows him to contribute without needing as much time to adjust.

That was evident in San Francisco's Week 10 win over the Dallas Cowboys, where Allen showed why his skill set could be valuable to the offense.

When healthy, the 49ers have one of the most talented offensive rosters in the NFL. Even with injuries creating challenges throughout the season, San Francisco remains a legitimate NFC contender.

Allen's ability to make an immediate impact gives Shanahan another experienced weapon to work with. If he can stay healthy and continue producing, he could become an important contributor as the 49ers pursue a deep postseason run.

articles.title: Steelers get good injury news on key offensive weapon
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. takes a major step toward returning from injured reserve ahead of Week 11.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles aren't the only team receiving positive injury updates, as the Pittsburgh Steelers received some encouraging news ahead of their Week 11 matchup against their interstate rival.

On Wednesday, head coach Mike McCarthy revealed that Steelers veteran wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr., in addition to three other previously injured players, will have their 21-day IR practice windows opened as they return to practice.

Pittman, who spent his first six years with the Indianapolis Colts , was traded to the Steelers in March 2026, where he was expected to form a fearsome wide receiver duo with DK Metcalf.

Unfortunately, Pittman suffered a foot injury early in the season, and it hampered his overall production. Pittman re-aggravated the injury during Week 5 practice and was subsequently placed on injured reserve, where he's missed the past five games.

Pittman's return to practice couldn't have come at a better time, as the Steelers' wide receiver woes hit an all-time low in last week's loss to the Cincinnati Bengals . But if the Steelers can indeed get Pittman back on the field in time for their Week 11 matchup against the Eagles, the Aaron Rodgers-led offense has a real shot at turning things around.

articles.title: Mississippi State Baseball’s 2027 Schedule Features Several Major SEC Showdowns
articles.summary: STARKVILLE, Miss. — Mississippi State baseball is preparing for another demanding season in the Southeastern Conference, with several notable matchups highli...
articles.body:
STARKVILLE, Miss. — Mississippi State baseball is preparing for another demanding season in the Southeastern Conference, with several notable matchups highlighting the Bulldogs' 2027 schedule.

The Diamond Dawgs will open their season Feb. 19 against Stony Brook at Dudy Noble Field. The three-game series begins a nine-game homestand as Mississippi State prepares for its second season under head coach Brian O'Connor.

Additionally, the Bulldogs will welcome several prominent SEC programs to Starkville, including Ole Miss, Oklahoma and Arkansas.

Mississippi State Opens With Nine Straight Home Games

Mississippi State will begin its 2027 campaign with an extended stretch at Dudy Noble Field.

Following the opening series against Stony Brook, the Bulldogs will host South Alabama on Feb. 23 and Jackson State on Feb. 24.

A three-game series against Saint Joseph's follows Feb. 26-28 before Troy visits Starkville on March 2.

The opening homestand provides Mississippi State with an opportunity to establish momentum before facing several challenging nonconference opponents.

Bulldogs Face National Competition in Arlington

Mississippi State's first road trip takes the program to Globe Life Field in Arlington, Texas, for the Amegy Bank College Baseball Series.

The Bulldogs will face Dallas Baptist on March 5, UCLA on March 6 and Wake Forest on March 7.

Those matchups offer Mississippi State an early opportunity to compete against nationally recognized baseball programs.

Furthermore, the Bulldogs will visit Southern Miss on March 9 before facing West Florida in Biloxi on March 10.

Mississippi State then returns home for a three-game series against North Alabama from March 12-14.

The Bulldogs will open their SEC schedule March 19 against Missouri at Dudy Noble Field.

Mississippi State will host the Tigers for three games before traveling to Georgia for its first conference road series March 25-27.

However, one of the most anticipated weekends arrives shortly afterward.

Ole Miss visits Starkville for a three-game series April 1-3, bringing one of college baseball's most recognizable rivalries back to Dudy Noble Field.

The Bulldogs will also face their in-state rivals April 27 in the annual Governor's Cup game in Pearl, Mississippi.

Oklahoma and Arkansas Highlight Home Schedule

Mississippi State's conference home schedule includes several difficult opponents beyond Ole Miss.

Texas A&M visits Starkville from April 16-18, while defending national champion Oklahoma arrives April 30 for a three-game series.

The Bulldogs will conclude their regular season at home against Arkansas from May 20-22.

Those matchups could carry considerable importance as Mississippi State competes for positioning in the SEC standings.

Meanwhile, the Bulldogs will face challenging conference road trips against Florida, Vanderbilt, Tennessee and LSU.

Mississippi State's Road to the SEC Tournament

The 2027 SEC Tournament is scheduled for May 25-30 at Hoover Metropolitan Stadium in Hoover, Alabama.

Before reaching that point, Mississippi State must navigate a 30-game conference schedule featuring 10 three-game series.

The Bulldogs will also play 35 regular-season home games, giving their supporters numerous opportunities to watch the program at Dudy Noble Field.

Mississippi State enters the new season following a 2026 campaign that produced 43 victories and an NCAA super regional appearance.

Now, O'Connor will look to build on that foundation as the Diamond Dawgs pursue another postseason run.

With a demanding schedule and several marquee opponents visiting Starkville, Mississippi State faces an important spring in 2027.

articles.title: With Sonny Gray, Twins should have an elite rotation (if there's a season)
articles.summary: Sonny Gray. Joe Ryan. Pablo Lopez. Taj Bradley. A high-level competition for the fifth spot. The Twins might be in business.
articles.body:
The Twins made a big, surprising, pre-lockout splash in free agency on Wednesday when they signed veteran right-handed pitcher Sonny Gray , bringing back a key member of their 2022 and '23 teams.

It's reportedly a two-year, $55 million deal, with an opt-out clause after the first year. $27.5 million is the third-highest average annual value on a contract in Twins history, behind only the two contracts they gave to Carlos Correa earlier this decade.

Between bringing back Gray out of nowhere and keeping catcher Ryan Jeffers on a one-year, $23 million qualifying offer, the Twins and owner Tom Pohlad are showing a meaningful commitment to spending on next year's team. Now they just need the league and the players association to agree on a new CBA at some point, so the season actually happens.

If there's an eventual agreement to be had and baseball to be played, the Twins should have one of the best starting rotations in the league. Here's what it could look like, along with the stats for each player's most recent season.

RHP Joe Ryan: 3.79 ERA, 159 K in 144.2 IP

RHP Sonny Gray: 2.72 ERA, 149 K in 169 IP (Red Sox)

RHP Pablo Lopez: 2.74 ERA, 73 K in 75.2 IP (2025)

RHP Taj Bradley: 3.73 ERA, 205 K in 178.1 IP

RHP Dean Kremer: 4.68 ERA, 86 K in 90.1 IP (Orioles/Twins)

Ryan struggled in the second half last season, but he's made two straight AL All-Star teams and is clearly a front-of-the-rotation starter when healthy and on his game. His fastball has a deceptive shape that makes it hard to hit, and his secondary offerings have only gotten better over the years.

Gray was 18-5 for Boston last season and finished fifth in AL Cy Young voting. The last time he was in Minnesota, he had a 2.79 ERA and finished as the Cy Young runner-up on a 2023 Twins team that made the playoffs. He's 37 years old but still seems to have plenty of gas in the tank.

Lopez missed all of last season with a UCL tear and also dealt with some injuries the year before that. If he can stay healthy, he's a frontline starter in his own right. Like Gray, he was an All-Star in 2023, when he struck out 234 batters (the most by a Twins pitcher since Johan Santana). Lopez was outstanding in 2025 when he was on the field.

Bradley is the Twins' reigning pitcher of the year. He had a breakout season with Minnesota, showcasing elite strikeout stuff with a four-pitch mix led by a fastball that touches triple-digit velocity. Bradley did give up plenty of hard contact, but he turns 26 next March and could still get better.

Kremer was struggling with the Orioles when he was acquired by the Twins. After the deal, the veteran had a 3.48 ERA and a sub-1 WHIP for Minnesota.

Adding to the projected quality of the Twins' rotation is the fact that there's some very intriguing depth, as well as potential competition for the fifth spot. Until now, we haven't even mentioned Bailey Ober, Mick Abel, Zebby Matthews, Connor Prielipp, or Kendry Rojas.

It's possible that not everyone in that group will be on the roster next year (Ober is a trade or non-tender candidate after a tough season). Others could be moved to the bullpen, where they could potentially thrive. But Abel and Prielipp, in particular, showed enough flashes last season to think they could compete with Kremer for the fifth spot. Abel seemed to be in the process of breaking out before an injury ended his season.

They Gray addition is an exciting one for the Twins. If the league can get past this looming lockout, Minnesota could be poised to be very competitive in the American League next year — with starting pitching leading the way.

articles.title: Gotham FC forward Jordynn Dudley wins NWSL Rookie of the Year
articles.summary: It wasn’t the type of stage Jordynn Dudley is used to climbing. Fresh off winning the 2023 national championship with Florida State, she walked past former V...
articles.body:
It wasn't the type of stage Jordynn Dudley is used to climbing.

Fresh off winning the 2023 national championship with Florida State, she walked past former Vice President Kamala Harris to a podium at the center of the White House South Portico. Dressed in a white suit, Dudley overcame her nerves to address the crowd of fellow national champions.

"I was terrified," Dudley recalls with a laugh. "I'm not someone to give speeches, especially in front of that many people. So, it was really scary, but I'm glad I got to do it."

Dudley doesn't cower from pressure, especially on the pitch. But this moment in 2024 was different. She knew this was "not a normal thing that people get to do," so she leaned on her teammates. Others from her freshman class gathered in their hotel room the night before to help write her speech .

It was, of course, a "big moment" for Dudley, who on Wednesday returned to Washington, D.C, in a very different capacity.

Dudley was one of 21 players and three coaches nominated for end-of-year NWSL Awards. The Gotham forward won Rookie of the Year in a category that also featured Houston Dash's Kat Rader and the San Diego Wave FC's Mimi Van Zanten. The honor comes despite her season being cut short by a foot fracture around October.

The Gotham forward had a breakout year, scoring four goals and recording three assists across 25 matches. She missed the latter part of the year after hurting her foot in training. At 5 feet 11 inches tall, she quickly meshed with Gotham's experienced roster, which includes U.S. women's national team players Rose Lavelle, Midge Purce, Jaedyn Shaw, Jaelin Howell, Tierna Davidson and Emily Sonnett. At the start of the year, she also played alongside Spain international and World Cup winner Esther Gonzalez, who later left the club, as well as a slew of international stars including former Chelsea attacking duo Sam Kerr and Guro Reiten.

"It's obviously a big transition from college to pro, so I had to get used to that, and thankfully had my whole team, my teammates, and the staff to help me get comfortable pretty quickly," Dudley told The Athletic in a recent interview.

Dudley fell into soccer as many kids do. Her parents signed her up for a youth team, and she fell in love.

"I just was having fun for the longest time," she said. "I wasn't looking to play in the future or whatever. I was just having fun, and I turned out to be good at it. It just happened."

She was a two-sport athlete, playing basketball through her senior year of high school. Growing up in Milton, Ga., she played against rival North Carolina Courage's Riley Jackson. She also looked up to Sonnett, who is from the area, too. At Florida State, 26-year-old Gotham teammate and FSU alum Jaelin Howell inspired her.

Dudley only played three seasons in college before deciding to go pro. She was a highly-rated prospect in the offseason, but ultimately landed at Gotham because "they had confidence in me and they could see what kind of player I could be and get more out of me." It helped that the roster was filled with experience.

"Jaelin (Howell) is one of the most important people on our team, and I watched her before I got to Florida State and knew how good of a player she was and how much she works. That also drew me to Gotham," Dudley said. "At Florida State, I feel like everyone that goes there has like a very similar mindset about winning and that really shows in her and how she plays."

Dudley has stayed around the team, despite her season-ending injury. By early November, she was still in a boot, rehabbing to strengthen her body before she could walk and return to the field. This was a week after Gotham won the club's first NWSL Shield.

Though Dudley missed the final games leading up to clinching the Shield, she was a vital part of Gotham's attack and helped them reach this milestone. With each week of her rookie campaign, Dudley visibly grew more confident in her role. She became a target for opponents and was often on the receiving end of fouls. Her speed and tactical ability make her extremely dangerous when barreling toward defenders.

"She makes the difference," head coach Juan Carlos Amoros said in September, following Dudley's first NWSL brace against the Courage. "We spoke before the game that she can win the games if she stays in the game. It's very difficult because, again, I don't know today how many fouls she suffered, and she needs to navigate that side of the game."

Her first goal came after dribbling through a crowd of North Carolina players and firing past another defender and keeper. The second was Gotham's game-winner, scored in stoppage time to end the match with a 2-1 win over the Courage.

"Both of her goals, one obviously is fantastic technical ability, but then the second one as well, it shows her personality and winning mentality to get that. That second goal in the 91st minute shows a lot of her character," Amoros said. "We are incredibly proud of her. She definitely made a difference today, and throughout the year, so we couldn't be happier with her."

Dudley's form earned her another call-up to the U-23 women's national team for their recent October camp at U.S. Soccer's new national training center near Atlanta. However, she was later recalled after being injured. She played one more game after her first brace and has been sidelined since.

At the time, Amoros was tight-lipped about Dudley's prognosis, though he told reporters she was "definitely our Rookie of the Year." The team confirmed her season-ending injury on Oct. 12, with Gotham's president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West echoing Amoros on Dudley's significance to the team after they clinched the Shield at Sports Illustrated Stadium on Nov. 1.

"She's been unbelievable, a real game changer for us, and she's there every moment of the day alongside the players now, even though she can't step on the field," Averbuch West said. "You saw her today with her teammates (on stage to receive the Shield), and so she's putting in the work to get back and be healthy."

Dudley is among a string of players whose 2026 campaigns were cut short at Gotham. Defender Bruninha suffered a knee injury while on international duty with Brazil in October. Defender Kayla Duran also suffered a knee injury at the start of the year. In July, Sonnett was ruled out for the rest of the season after rupturing her patellar tendon and requiring surgery.

Despite the injury, Dudley said being around the team as often as possible is important to her.

"It's different (being injured), but at the same time, I wasn't the loudest person in the locker room in the first place. So, I'm there as, like, small support, cheering everyone on in the box upstairs and high-fiving in the locker room, that kind of stuff," Dudley said. "The presence of me being there helps me as well, because I don't want to be away from the team."

Dudley now looks forward to her return, not just for Gotham but to the U-23 women's national team as she works toward her first call-up to the senior team. U.S. head coach Emma Hayes called Dudley "a young prospect who's had a great year" in late September, around the time of her injury, and said she looked forward to seeing her with the U-23s.

"It's such a good opportunity to be called up to the U23s," Dudley said. "The talent is amazing, and it's such a high level. It's been really good to be able to go to a couple of those camps and get feedback from the coaching staff, both the 23s and the full team coaching staff, to know what I can do to get myself closer to the full team, because that is one of my goals eventually.

"Staying consistent once I get back on the field, (and) getting called into camps, that'll help me grow my confidence and develop myself more to be a more complete player."

Though Dudley's season was cut short, she has left her mark in the NWSL and now has hardware to show for it.

Since that moment at the White House stage, she went on to win another national championship in 2025 and turned pro. In her rookie campaign, she won a Challenge Cup, NWSL Shield, earned two NWSL Player of the Month nominations, and now Rookie of the Year. She has no plans to slow down and will continue leaning on her teammates when she needs them most.

"Most of my success here has come from my teammates," Dudley says. "They've helped me grow in so many ways, telling me so many different things, helping me learn the league and different players and how to go against different players, and I owe everything to them."

articles.title: In the land of Frankenstein, Gukesh asked to distance himself from 'what people are saying' ahead of World Chess Championship
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In 1815, Mount Tambora in Indonesia unleashed one of the most violent volcanic eruptions in recorded history.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In 1815, Mount Tambora in Indonesia unleashed one of the most violent volcanic eruptions in recorded history. Though its fury didn't stay buried in Indonesia. Ash and sulphur soon climbed into the atmosphere, altering weather patterns across the globe. Europe turned cold, wet and grey. The year 1816 would go down in history as the Year Without a Summer.It was summer by the calendar, but nothing about it felt that way. A group of young English writers and intellectuals, Mary Godwin, who would later become Mary Shelley; her partner Percy Bysshe Shelley; the famous poet Lord Byron; his physician and fellow writer John Polidori; and Mary's stepsister Claire Clairmont, found themselves holidaying at Villa Diodati, Byron's rented residence overlooking Lake Geneva in Cologny, Switzerland.Confined indoors by relentless rain and gloom, it was Byron who proposed they pass the dreary evenings with a ghost-story competition, each of them tasked with conjuring something frightening enough to unsettle the rest.Initially, Mary struggled to find her idea, until a dream supposedly handed her one. It was a short story that would eventually swell into one of the most influential novels in the history of literature, Frankenstein.Picture it for a moment. Some of the greatest literary minds of the Romantic era, trapped indoors by foul weather, daring each other to invent something terrifying.That said, Frankenstein wasn't even the only invention born that night. Polidori's own short work of prose fiction, The Vampyre, emerged from the very same contest.That one meeting in Cologny, 210 years ago, revolutionised literature by launching modern science fiction, reshaping Gothic horror, and creating the modern vampire archetype.And now, in that same corner of Switzerland, something with the potential to leave a similarly lasting mark on the game of 64 squares is about to unravel. In a battle of 20-year-olds, India's Gukesh Dommaraju will take on Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov for the World Chess Championship crown, in Geneva's Cologny, from November 24 to December 12.The last time Switzerland hosted a World Championship was in 2004, when Vladimir Kramnik met Peter Leko in Brissago. It was a historic match in its own right, but that's a story for another day, because this time, Leko returns to Swiss soil not as a challenger but as a witness.A lesson from the World Championship"I learned a lot from that (2004 World Championship) experience. Going into a World Championship match, you have to distance yourself from all the expectations and from what people are saying," Leko, known to be one of the most respected voices in the world of chess, told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive conversation. Leko, who will share the official commentary duties with Russian Grandmaster Peter Svidler for the 2026 FIDE World Chess Championship, didn't need long to find a parallel from the reigning champion's own past."I would also like to relate this to Gukesh's match against Ding Liren," he said. "I felt that one of the reasons Gukesh lost the first game was the incredible hype surrounding him before the match."It wasn't hard to see why that hype had built."He had a fantastic run, qualified for the Candidates, delivered a phenomenal performance at the Chess Olympiad, and his rating was booming. Ding Liren's rating was going down while Gukesh's was skyrocketing. Everybody was expecting Gukesh to crush Ding Liren," he recalled.That weight of expectation, in Leko's reading, pushed Gukesh into a trap of his own making."I think Gukesh went into that first game feeling that he had to show the whole world that he was the hunter and that he wanted to dominate the match. It backfired with that terrible loss," the 47-year-old Grandmaster explained.The rest, as chess fans will remember, turned into one of the most dramatic title matches in recent memory."That already signalled that it was going to be a hell of a match. And it certainly was a rollercoaster, which Gukesh eventually managed to win under dramatic circumstances."Why the pressure has switched sidesIf Gukesh walked into Singapore carrying the world's expectations, Leko believes he'll walk into Cologny carrying almost none of them; and that, this time, it's Sindarov who has to live with being the favourite."The expectations are now completely opposite," the Hungarian said. "Sindarov is the one who has had an incredible year, winning the World Cup in Goa, winning the Candidates, playing fantastic chess with the Uzbek team and winning the Chess Olympiad. He carries the expectations."Gukesh, by contrast, gets to play the role he was denied last time."I believe that, from Gukesh's side, he doesn't care too much about the outside noise. He just wants to focus on himself and show the whole world, as well as himself, that he is capable of retaining his title and playing a fantastic match against Sindarov." Which, Leko says, sets up something close to a mirror image of the match he's already seen up close. "In this respect, I'm expecting a very close fight, just like the match between Ding and Gukesh two years ago."Fourteen games much better for the match?There's a structural significance to this match too, one that's easy to miss amid the psychological drama. When Kramnik met Leko in Brissago in 2004, it was a 14-game match. The cycles that followed shrank the format to 12 games, and it stayed that way for the best part of two decades until Magnus Carlsen's defence against Ian Nepomniachtchi in 2021 restored it to 14.Gukesh and Sindarov will now play out that same 14-game format in Cologny. And Leko, unsurprisingly, is thrilled to see the longer format back."One other thing I'm extremely happy about is that the World Championship matches are back to 14 games, as they were last time. In between, we had those 12-game matches. I believe 14 games is much better for a World Championship match," the veteran Grandmaster, also coach of Germany's Vincent Keymer, opined."It means that the players are finally pushed to give absolutely everything they have. There is an enormous amount of preparation, tremendous tension and some crazy games. By the end, the players are completely exhausted."After all, this is about the title and becoming World Champion. You then have to play two additional games, the 13th and 14th. Those games are already extremely demanding because you're tired and exhausted, yet you still have to find incredible strength within yourself to keep delivering your absolute best in the final game."A storyteller's seat in the 2026 World Chess ChampionshipAsked whether he's looking forward to commentating on the match, Leko's answer came without a beat of hesitation."Incredibly, I'm so happy. It's like a dream come true for me," he told this website. "I've already done commentary during World Championship matches, but only for a few games. With all my experience, I know exactly that a World Championship match is about so much more than moves and individual games. It's a whole story. Every small mosaic piece put together establishes the bigger picture of the match."As a commentator, together with Svidler, we'll have the opportunity, right from the beginning, to bring our audience into this magical world of the World Championship match. We'll be able to explain all the psychological moments, the expectations before the match and how everything surrounding the event has a huge impact. Then come the first game, every single move, the opening decisions, what we expect might happen and what makes sense from the players' teams' perspectives for the future."I think it will be a fantastic opportunity to go into real depth, not just commentate on the games and the moves, but tell the whole story. I'm really looking forward to a dramatic finish in this match."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Alabama QB Keelon Russell's mother sues Marriott over twin's death, hotel counters with 911 audio
articles.summary: April Moore says a hotel worker knocked during CPR and no AED was available as she sues Marriott International over daughter Kierston Russell's death.
articles.body: April Moore, mother of Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell, is suing AC Hotel Tuscaloosa Downtown and Marriott International over the death of her daughter, Kierston Russell. Details of the wrongful death suit surfaced ahead of a Dec. 7 hearing in Tuscaloosa County Circuit Court. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Russell has thrown for nearly 2,500 yards and 21 touchdowns this season. Off the field, his family is pursuing a jury trial over the events of June 3, 2025. Kierston, his 18-year-old twin sister, planned to enroll at Alabama alongside him. Per defense filings, Moore and Keelon left their room around 7:20 p.m. after Kierston reported stomach pain and irregular sleep. Moore returned, found Kierston unresponsive on the bathroom floor, called 911 at 9:55 p.m., and started CPR. Kierston died at DCH Regional Medical Center. TWO MEN DIE AFTER SUSPECTED ELECTROCUTION AT HOTEL POOL AS RESCUE EFFORT INJURES OTHERS Moore sued on June 15, 2026, accusing the hotel and Marriott of failing to train staff in CPR or provide a defibrillator. Her complaint states a worker knocked on the door during the emergency, forcing Moore to stop compressions to answer it, and offered no aid. Plaintiff's attorney Derrick Mills said experts believe an AED would have saved Kierston's life, adding the hotel "literally frustrated April's efforts in trying to revive her daughter." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The defense disputes that account using timestamps. In court filings, the defendants say 911 dispatchers never called the front desk, and staff responded only after a guest reported screaming. They contend 911 audio shows Moore never stopped CPR to open the door, requiring a worker to unlock it with a master key before EMTs began treatment within three minutes. The defense also says 911 calls and bodycam photos place an AED in the room within three to five minutes, adding Alabama law did not require one. Defense counsel Rebecca Young declined comment. FORMER CLEVELAND BROWNS WR DAVID BELL SEEKS $300M AFTER BOTCHED SURGERY ALLEGEDLY NEARLY KILLED HIM To reach a jury under Alabama law, Moore must clear two hurdles: proving the hotel owed a duty beyond summoning paramedics, and proving its response cost Kierston her life. Marriott and the hotel requested dismissal in October; Moore moved to seal records and filed a non-public response on Nov. 6, setting up a Dec. 7 showdown in court. articles.title: VJ Edgecombe stars in Sixers’ comeback win over Orlando Magic
articles.summary: VJ Edgecombe’s all-around brilliance led the Sixers to an unbelievable 121-116 win over the Orlando Magic, pushing Philadelphia to a 13-3 record despite the...
articles.body:
VJ Edgecombe's all-around brilliance led the Sixers to an unbelievable 121-116 win over the Orlando Magic, pushing Philadelphia to a 13-3 record despite the absences of Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, and Dean Wade.

Without the services of Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, and Dean Wade, this was always going to be an uphill battle for the Sixers. They made sure to put themselves in a hole early, naturally, to make it as difficult as possible before they stumbled into a few things that worked.

Healthy or not, the Sixers played some atrocious defense to start the game, allowing the Magic to drop 40 points in the opening quarter thanks to haphazard closeouts and pitiful defensive rebounding. It felt like nearly every Orlando make was a dunk or a three on a second-chance play, and the reinforcements from the bench were among the worst culprits. Justin Edwards got a rare chance to play and immediately showed why he has been buried on the bench, losing his man on the weak side time after time after time.

They were able to battle back from that slow start thanks in large part to the guys at the top of the depth chart. LeBron James dropped the playmaking-first mentality he has had within this star-studded group and got to work immediately as a scorer, hitting a three on their first possession to kickstart a 14-point half where he did a lot of at-rim attacking and paint scoring. Leveraging his size advantage on some of Orlando's smaller defenders, he hit a few touch shots from around 10 feet and in, later using the threat of one to hit Tacko Fall for a lobbed entry and a dunk.

Oh, right, Tacko Fall played real minutes on Wednesday! With Philadelphia in a big hole and in search of any kind of spark, Fall got a chance and took advantage of it, sitting deep in a 2-3 Sixers zone to dissuade anyone who got remotely close to the basket. The shift put him in a great position to succeed, and Fall picked up two blocks and dissuaded other potential shot attempts on Magic drives, helping the Sixers stabilize on that end of the floor. It was a smart adjustment from Nurse that almost immediately brought them back within reach of the lead. And his strong play carried into the second half: the Magic repeatedly beat Philadelphia's perimeter defense and then saw him at the rim and thought better of it

It helped that Joel Embiid woke up after a sleepy start to the game, too. Philadelphia played through him early to their own detriment, but Embiid kept hunting for quality shots rather than letting early misses cloud his mind, eventually breaking through. Without Maxey and Brown to space for, he played a lot of power offense in the post, dropping shots over the top of Wendell Carter Jr. from in tight. One of my favorite sequences of the game came when he missed a short post hook and reacted to the shot in flight before it had even hit the rim, beating both Carter and Franz Wagner to a rebound before depositing a layup plus the foul:

His offensive success led to increased energy on the defensive end, with Embiid picking up two blocks late in the second quarter on Carter attempts at the rim. The second was a particularly athletic play, Embiid flying in so late to deter Carter that the officials initially ruled it a foul before a successful Sixers challenge put him on the right side of history. As we hit halftime, Embiid and LeBron had combined for 30 first-half points, doing their part as leaders with so many absences in the lineup.

Philadelphia also got an excellent cameo from rookie guard Labaron Philon, who was comically helpless on one switch against Franz Wagner but otherwise hardly put a foot wrong. His pace and comfort at the point of attack scored him a couple of runners from the middle of the paint, and he capped off his best sequence of the season to date with a transition three from the corner. Those first half minutes showed the hybrid on-ball/off-ball impact that made him an appealing guard prospect, and I wouldn't mind seeing more of him in the weeks ahead.

For a good chunk of the second half, the Sixers were just one breakthrough play away from flipping the lead and never going back. The inexperience of their available roster showed up on a few occasions, like a VJ Edgecombe "save" under their basket that went into the hands of the Magic, or a Jabari Walker turnover that turned a promising transition possession into an Anthony Black three on the other end. The Sixers' zone defense did enough to bring the game close, but you could feel the loss of offensive firepower when Philadelphia had to respond themselves, as Orlando crowded Embiid and made it difficult for him to get to his spots and take over on offense.

But you knew that Edgecombe was going to have his moment in this game at some point, and as the second half wore on, it increasingly became his show to run on offense. He was at the controls in the pick-and-roll attack with Embiid as his partner, showing off the in-between game that grew exponentially in the second half of his rookie season. Edgecombe hit twisting shots from all over the floor, a twisting turnaround in the lane eventually morphing into a movement three while moving to his left, the sort of difficult, star-level shots we weren't even sure he would attempt after seeing how he approached his lone season at Baylor. But this, in so many words, is just what we expect from him these days:

Edgecombe's biggest contribution of the night finally turned the Sixers into frontrunners, with his movement in space forcing Franz Wagner into a difficult pull-up two that fell harmlessly off the rim. On the ensuing Sixers possession, Edgecombe drove down Orlando's lane and drew the help, firing a pass out to Jabari Walker in the corner for the biggest triple of the night.

From there, it was a matter of winning the possession-by-possession battle, and the Sixers leveraged all their crunch-time might to see this one out. Embiid's drop-heavy coverage was altered dramatically, the Sixers bringing him up to the level and switching behind it furiously, with KCP playing dogged defense to stay attached to Wagner even if it took four, five, or six efforts. LeBron was a short-roll demon for Philly in the clutch, scoring on the roll and finding shooters in the weakside corner whenever Orlando had the gall to send help his way.

And Edgecombe would need to come up big one more time, hitting the game's biggest shot on an are-you-kidding-me three with a hand in his face, moments before he would slap a loose ball off of Desmond Bane to secure another extra possession for Philadelphia.

A gutsy win if there ever was one, and it took just about everybody available on the roster.

Anfernee Simons had a big night as the Maxey replacement in the starting lineup, and it was very cool to see him hit the corner dagger playing in his hometown.

Kentavious Caldwell-Pope had what amounted to a one-man run in the middle of the third quarter, bailing the Sixers out of a couple of stagnant half-court possessions by sprinting through Embiid DHOs for midrange jumpers, punctuating the sequence with a trail three out of an Embiid post-up. It has been a joy to watch him on this team so far, because he has taken basically every shot they need him to and essentially no more than that. It is way harder than he has made it look to straddle the line of aggression as a role player.

Justin Edwards had the single worst shot attempt I have seen in my time watching basketball in the fourth quarter. Wide-open three that he missed by probably six feet. You'd have to try to miss by that much.

articles.title: WNBA launches search for next commissioner, but outgoing Cathy Engelbert could stay into 2027
articles.summary: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert says more than a dozen candidates are in the mix to succeed her, with officiating and player relations among top issues.
articles.body: The WNBA's search for Cathy Engelbert’s successor has officially kicked off. According to reports, the league will work to eventually narrow down a list of more than a dozen candidates. Engelbert’s eight-year, at-times tumultuous tenure is nearing its end, but she could remain in the role beyond 2026 if the search extends into 2027. Engelbert previously announced plans to retire at the end of the year but clarified that she would remain commissioner beyond Dec. 31 if a successor was not in place. She took over as commissioner in 2019. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Monday marked Engelbert’s final WNBA Board of Governors meeting. Representatives from all 15 current teams attended, along with officials from the three expansion franchises set to join the league over the next four years: Cleveland, Detroit and Philadelphia. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver also attended. That meeting came a few days after Engelbert met with coaches, general managers and team presidents last week at the WNBA offices for the annual competition committee meetings. If the WNBA chooses not to extend Engelbert’s tenure beyond Dec. 31, it could consider NBA Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum. Tatum served as interim WNBA commissioner for nine months before Engelbert was hired following Lisa Borders’ departure in 2018. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SAYS SHE'S TALKED WITH NBA COMMISSIONER ADAM SILVER AMID SEARCH FOR WNBA'S NEXT COMMISSIONER THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The next commissioner of the league will inherit a host of issues, including officiating, the transgender debate, scheduling and improving a strained relationship with players. The league thrived in many ways during Engelbert’s tenure. Under her leadership, the WNBA enjoyed record growth and popularity, and signed a record-breaking broadcasting deal. Players surpassed $1 million in annual salaries. WNBA EXPANDS REGULAR SEASON TO 50 GAMES STARTING IN 2027, THE LONGEST SCHEDULE IN LEAGUE HISTORY But despite her accomplishments, Engelbert’s relationship with players was cordial at best, confrontational at other times. New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart may have summed it up best when said players "respect" Engelbert. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Late last month, Engelbert presented the WNBA championship trophy to the Golden State Valkyries after they defeated the Atlanta Dream in the league’s first Finals series to reach seven games. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Kenya’s marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir gets three-year ban for doping
articles.summary: Jepchirchir breached anti-doping rules by testing positive for banned substance EPO, Athletics Integrity Unit says.
articles.body:
Kenya’s reigning world and former Olympic marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been suspended for three years after testing positive for the banned substance EPO, the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said.

Jepchirchir admitted to breaching anti-doping rules relating to the presence of a prohibited substance or its metabolites and to the use or attempted use of a prohibited substance or prohibited method, the AIU said in a statement on Thursday.

EPO, a synthetic form of erythropoietin, is a laboratory-made version of a natural hormone produced mainly by the kidneys that signals the bone marrow to make more red blood cells, according to the Mayo Clinic.

Athletes sometimes misuse synthetic EPO as a performance-enhancing drug to boost oxygen delivery to muscles and improve endurance.

Jepchirchir was provisionally suspended last month after the AIU, which investigates doping in track and field athletes on behalf of the sport’s governing body, World Athletics, returned an adverse analytical finding for EPO from an out-of-competition sample collected in Kenya before her Sydney Marathon victory in late August.

Jepchirchir has accepted the disqualification of all of her competitive results since July 17.

The 33-year-old won women’s marathon gold at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 and the world title last year. She is also a former world record holder in the half marathon.

The Sydney Marathon, which noted that Jepchirchir’s in-competition test had returned negative, said Irine Cheptai is set to be elevated to 2026 women’s champion.

The AIU said it also sanctioned two other high-profile Kenyan runners.

Veronica Loleo, a half-marathon silver medallist at the 2026 world road running championships, was banned for three years after testing positive for EPO in an out-of-competition test.

Meanwhile, Ronald Korir, who placed fourth in the 2023 Berlin Marathon, received a six-year ban after abnormalities were found in his athlete biological passport, which he failed to explain. The AIU analysed 20 blood samples taken from Korir from May 6, 2023, to August 18, 2025, and identified abnormalities.

“The Kenyan authorities have made a lot of progress in the fight against doping in the last five years, but these cases highlight that there is still a long way to go,” AIU chief executive Brett Clothier said in a statement.

“The Kenyan government is aware of the current situation and has committed to further strengthen the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya and take action to address the criminal networks that facilitate doping within the country.”

These were the latest in a long series of doping cases involving distance runners from Kenya.

Women’s marathon world record holder Ruth Chepng’etich, also from Kenya, was banned for three years in 2025 after admitting a charge related to a positive test for a banned diuretic. Former New York Marathon winner Albert Korir was given a five-year ban in March.

articles.title: Malaysian weightlifting champion Roslin loses arm after motorbike crash
articles.summary: Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin, who won a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games 2026, had his arm amputated after accident.
articles.body:
Malaysia’s Commonwealth Games gold medal-winning weightlifter Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin had his right arm amputated after a motorcycle accident but is in a stable condition in hospital, a Malaysian sports official said.

Roslin was “awake and smiling,” following a seven-hour-long surgery at Kuala Lumpur Hospital, Malaysia Weightlifting Federation president Ayub Rahmat told the AFP news agency on Thursday.

The 21-year-old was conscious and in a stable condition in hospital, three days after the crash, the country’s top weightlifting official said.

Roslin reportedly lost control of his motorcycle while riding on the expressway on Monday night and sustained injuries to his right leg and arm, a haematoma – pooled blood – in the neck, as well as minor head injuries, according to Malaysian media.

Doctors amputated Hafizuddin’s arm above the elbow, local media reports said.

“Physically, his condition is improving but this incident has had a great impact on his future,” Rahmat said. He called it “a shock and a huge loss” for weightlifting in the country.

The Malaysian government said it would cover all treatment costs.

“The government, through the [National Sports Council], is fully covering the costs of treatment and medical care related to the incident, including follow-up treatment and hospital accommodation until he is discharged,” the ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.

It added that Roslin’s training allowance would also continue at the current eligible rate.

Malaysian’s Sultan Idris Education University (UPSI) also offered psychological support and sports psychology intervention for Roslin as part of his recovery, Malaysian media reported.

“In this critical situation, an athlete’s greatest challenge is not merely the physical healing process, but also how to cope with emotional shock, the denial phase and the sudden loss of sporting identity,” said Dr Jaffry Zakaria, associate professor of the Faculty of Sports Science and Coaching (FSSK) at UPSI.

Hafizuddin won gold at this year’s Commonwealth Games in the men’s 88kg category and set a games record with a total lift of 345kg. His attempt of 162kg in the snatch category set a national record as well as a games record.

He was a prospect for the country at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.

articles.title: Trey White's second-half surge sparks Texas Tech football pass rush
articles.summary: Trey White's track record shows he's a top-notch pass rusher. The Texas Tech football team had to wait out his August injury to see it.
articles.body:
The Texas Tech football staff fished Trey White from the NCAA transfer portal last winter, expecting him to make up, if not all, at least a chunk of the production Romello Height gave the Red Raiders from the same position.

Keep up his recent pace and White might get there yet.

The Red Raiders' 6-foot-2, 250-pound edge defender has four sacks in the past three games, giving him six sacks for the season. Within the Big 12, the fifth-year senior from San Diego is tied for fifth in sacks but tied for second in sacks per game at 0.75, an indication of the time he missed.

Our best photos of Texas Tech football's preseason camp practices

White suffered a knee injury the last week of preseason practice, underwent surgery on Sept. 1 and made his season debut in Tech's Sept. 18 victory against Houston. He had only two sacks through the Red Raiders' first seven games, but recently has looked like the player they expected.

"I've been a hundred percent healthy the past few weeks, so that's felt really good," White said on Tuesday, Nov. 17, "and obviously, I've seen it in my game play as well. Just getting more comfortable with the scheme and the defense has been really helpful. And definitely being healthy helps a lot."

White spent his first four college years at San Diego State. He earned first-team all-conference recognition each of the past two years with composite numbers of 113 tackles, including 29 tackles for loss and 19 1/2 sacks. Among active FBS players, he's fourth in career sacks with 25 1/2 and eighth in tackles for loss with 38.

"Trey has a really unique bend to him," Tech coach Joey McGuire said. "I think that's contributed to the amount of sacks he's had in his career."

The Tech pass rush lacks the star power of last year's team. Gone are David Bailey and Height, who accounted for 24 sacks. Yet, this year's Red Raiders have 32 sacks, on pace to break the school record of 41 set in 2009 and tied in 2025.

Holmes leads the Big 12 with 8 sacks. After White and his 6 sacks, freshman edge defender LaDamion Guyton has 5 and defensive tackle Mateen Ibirogba has 3 1/2.

White's untimely injury added another layer of complication to what any first-year transfer into a program faces. But White's catching up.

"I think it's just the opportunity to get better every single day here has been helping me a lot," he said, "and the competition that we face is best in the nation, so just going against the best competition — we have the best O-line, the best tackles — so going against them throughout the spring and fall camp has only gotten me better.

"And being able to do some different things in the defense that I'm not used to doing, but it shows my versatility for the next level has really helped me a lot."

The Tech front four's been ferocious lately, and White's sacks have come in high-leverage situations. In a 34-26 victory against Arizona, he sacked Noah Fifita on third down in the red zone, making the Wildcats settle for a field goal. Ibirogba flushed Fifita from the pocket, and White tripped him up.

In a 53-48 victory against West Virginia, White's sack with 1:53 left resulted in a turnover on downs and preserved a 51-48 lead. Holmes and Guyton flushed quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. from the pocket in White's direction.

The Mountaineers got the ball back and White tackled Hawkins for a safety for the game's final points. Ibirogba collapsed the pocket and White finished the play.

In the Red Raiders' 52-27 conquest of Oklahoma State last week, White had a sack on third down, forcing a punt late in the third quarter with Tech leading 35-20. Ibirogba hemmed in OSU quarterback Drew Mestemaker and White brought him down.

Tech snapped Mestemaker's streak of eight consecutive games with 300 yards passing.

"I thought our pass rush, first, second, third and fourth down was great," defensive coordinator Shiel Wood said. "Really made them uncomfortable."

articles.title: Who will win? Sarasota, Manatee Week 2 football playoff previews, picks
articles.summary: Previews and predictions for high school football playoff games played by Sarasota, Manatee area teams on Thursday, Nov. 19, and Friday, Nov. 20, 2026.
articles.body:
Here are the previews and predictions for FHSAA and FIT high school football playoff games played by Sarasota and Manatee area schools on Thursday, Nov. 19, and Friday, Nov. 20, 2026.

Bayshore at Wellen Park high school football game photo gallery

Analysis: In its inaugural season, Wellen Park made the FIT and will play a Belleville team ranked 300th in Florida. Wellen Park averages 323.6 yards per game, while Belleville averages 278.6. The two teams are evenly matched. Wellen Park will need to overcome the road challenge, which it has done several times this season.

No. 5 North Marion (2-8) at No. 4 Bayshore (3-7)

Bayshore Bruins defend their home turf against the Southeast Seminoles

Analysis: Bayshore hasn't made a playoff appearance since 2005, but thanks to Florida's playoff expansion last fall, the Bruins made the FIT. North Marion is ranked 344th in Florida compared to Bayshore's 335th spot. The Bruins average 307.2 yards per game, while North Marion manages only 162.3. With home advantage and a better offense, Bayshore has the chance to advance to the regional finals.

No. 4 Plant City (9-2) at No. 1 Riverview (9-2)

Analysis: Riverview defeated Haines City 52-28 on the road in Friday's regional quarterfinal. Quarterback Logan Carrillo went 12-of-16, throwing for 188 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. Running back Justin Flores scored two touchdowns, rushing for 47 yards on nine carries. Receiver Trenton Huffman also had two scores, recording 84 yards behind six receptions. Plant City is ranked 119th in Florida. Riverview averages 460.8 total yards per game, while Plant City manages 289.3. While Plant City has a strong defense that allows an average of 10.7 points per game, Riverview's offense has more than enough strength to overcome it.

No. 3 Palmetto (10-1) at No. 2 Tampa Bay Tech (10-1)

Analysis: Palmetto defeated Royal Palm Beach 23-7 in the regional quarterfinal on Friday, marking its 10th straight win. The Tigers led 10-7 for most of the game before three-star cornerback Nazir Pitchford (UNC commit) had a pick-six, breaking open the game. With 6:52 left, the Tigers marched downfield before Shane Partridge sealed Palmetto's win with a 2-yard score. Tampa Bay Tech is ranked 44th in Florida and is evenly matched with Palmetto. The two teams both average 365 yards per game on offense. The Tigers have a slight edge on defense, averaging 69.3 tackles compared to Tampa Bay Tech's 57.7. Tampa Bay Tech is led by sophomore quarterback Martavius Conway Jr., who has thrown for 1,767 yards, 17 touchdowns and five interceptions this season, completing 60.1 percent of his passes. articles.title: How Player's Era became college basketball premier early season tournament
articles.summary: In just three years, Player's Era has become the top November destination for the biggest men's basketball contenders, and it's not hard to see why.
articles.body:
Not even Seth Berger thought his wildest idea could become what it today.

The entrepreneur and high school basketball coach wanted to add to the long list of multi-team men's college basketball events that take place around Thanksgiving, hoping to recreate the excitement of March Madness in November. He and EverWonder Studio CEO Ian Orefice sought parties interested in bringing it to life.

Three years later, the Player's Era Festival is the biggest regular-season event in the sport.

The year's tournament in Las Vegas is its largest yet, with its 24 participant split into the Player's Era 8 (Nov. 17-19) and the Player's Era 16 (Nov. 24-28), with half of the field in the USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll .

A rapid growth, and one Berger doesn't see halting soon, becoming the destination teams across the country want to be in the first month of the season.

One can't just whip up a major tournament off a whim. It took financial backing from EverWonder and its parent company RedBird to help kickstart the conversation with MGM, which agreed to host the event at its arena.

That paved the way for coaches to be intrigued at the idea of participating in this new event, which offered name, image and likeness opportunities. Questions were raised about the festival's viability in an unprecedented era of college sports.

"People had to believe: could we actually operate an event?" Berger told USA TODAY Sports. "We had to be able to answer for the coaches themselves because they're looking out for their kids."

See who dominates Nielsen's list of top college basketball fan bases

The first edition in 2024 featured eight teams, with Oregon winning the inaugural crown. The field more than doubled to 18 in 2025 under an odd format that saw eventual national champion Michigan take the title.

There was no doubt Player's Era established itself as the premier tournament, setting up for another loaded future. That was solidified when it reached agreement with ESPN on a multi-year broadcasting deal ahead of the 2026-27 season with the field expanded to 24.

It could have been larger. Organizers had to decline teams from participating.

"I would not be exaggerating if I told you that every week, I get three or four coaches or GMs reaching out, wanting to be in Players Era," Berger said.

How teams were chosen was a combination on trying to make schedules make sense for teams while able to "create some potential compelling matchups." With so many teams, organizers felt it was easier to split it into two weeks rather than one gigantic field.

The tournament also did away from the confusing record and point differential determination for the championship rounds, opting with a traditional bracket to make it simpiler.

Player's Era thrives, but are there concerns?

All 24 teams receive than $1 million guarantees for participating, with it varying among the field. Kansas is one of the top earners with $3.1 million, according to Sportico . Winners of the tournament also get a guaranteed $300,000, with runner-up at $200,000, according to a Players Era spokesperson.

"We have no shortage of schools that are interested, and it makes sense, right?" Berger said. "We're filling a lot of gaps for them, both from a financial perspective as well as a competitive standpoint."

The tournament works in the era of NIL, when teams are trying to collect funds in any way it can. In just three years, the quality of fields has overwhelmed traditional Thankgiving week events the Maui Invitational and Battle 4 Atlantis, which has caused mixed reactions from college basketball purists.

What's added to the cause is a concerning problem in the sports: empty arenas. Albiet much smaller venues, the Lahaina Civic Center in Hawaii and Imperial Arena in the Bahamas are filled, while events around the continental U.S. have often had more open seats than occupied ones.

It's happened early in the Player's Era 8 at Michelob Ultra Arena. Ahead of the tournament, Berger said a reason for why this has been such an issue is because the "broader economy" impacting financial situations, but remained hopeful the arenas would be packed. In 2026, Player's Era also paid for spirit squads and mascots to make the trip.

"We've seen pretty strong sales for Players Era, so we're expecting pretty good environments," he said. "The challenge is always is the same: is first and foremost creating a first-class environment for for the teams and the players and the coaches and their staffs, and everything starts there, right? And then separately, you want to create an amazing environment for the fans."

Player's Era is really banking on the caliber of teams to help with that. With so many ranked teams, Berger compares this tournament to what the Sweet 16 and Elite Eight could look like in March, and the intensity helping raise the atmosphere within the arenas.

If the event succeeds again, Berger envisions a future where Player's Era continues to expand where basically a calendar can be created for it, adding more events to the early season. It also hosts a women's edition (Dec. 19-20) in and helped organized the Eternal City Tip-Off between Villanova and Notre Dame to start the season.

It being where another title begins would certainly ensure that.

"It's really possible that one of the teams that wins the Players' Era 8 or 16 is going to move on to win a national championship in April, again," Berger said.

articles.title: Calkins Conquerors prepare to tip-off boys basketball season
articles.summary: Under the direction of veteran head coach Lane Jones, the Calkins Conquerors boys varsity basketball team tips-off the season Nov. 20 at Fairview.
articles.body:
DAMASCUS TWP. — The Calkins boys varsity basketball team got off to a slow start last year, managing just one win in the first six games of the 2025-26 campaign.

However, the Conquerors obviously learned from their mistakes and improved steadily as the season progressed. By the time it was all over, they'd racked up 14 wins and advanced all the way to the NPCA tournament semifinals.

"We went 1-5 in those early games last year, but I think we gained valuable experience by playing tough teams from Pennsylvania , Delaware and Ohio," head coach Lane Jones said.

The good news for local fans is that Calkins returns a deep and talented roster after losing just two players to graduation. And while the absence of Peter Race and Gideon Madden will be keenly felt, Jones thinks this team is poised for a deep playoff run.

"I believe we have the talent to compete with anyone on our schedule," the veteran skipper said. "But, it's up to us to show the grit and tenacity necessary to earn wins against solid competition."

The Conquerors are scheduled to open their season Friday, Nov. 20, at the Fairview Tip-Off Tournament. Action gets underway at 2 p.m. in Reading.

Calkins battled its way to an overall record of 14-9 last season while also honing its skills with four scrimmages against non-league opponents.

The Conquerors hope to improve upon that mark by combining quickness in the backcourt with impressive size in the post.

Sophomore Nehemiah Sheridan returns at point guard and will be joined on the perimeter by classmate Sam Madden.

"Nehemiah started last year as a freshman and he's showing great improvement," Jones said. "And Sam has grown so much in his abilities during the off-season. I expect him to grow and mature even more with experience."

Meanwhile the Conquerors' will be physically imposing in paint. Senior center Matt Black (6-3) anchors the low post along with junior forwards Deegan Cahoon (6-4) and Spencer Arendt (6-2).

Sophomore Dan Schelling (6-2) and freshman Landon Buselli (6-2) will also contribute key minutes, as will underclassmen Landon Buselli and Sawyer Buselli.

Calkins hits the hardwood for the first time Nov. 20 at Fairview. The Conquerors will be tested right away with early games against both teams that finished ahead of them at the season-ending NPCA tournament.

"I feel that we have the talent this year to play for the championship," Jones said. "But we need to need to grow in tenacity, physicality and skills. The other teams are not standing still."

Jones has been coaching varsity level boys basketball for nearly three decades.

He started his career at North Pocono Christian Academy, then took time off to help raise his own children.

Jones returned to the sideline in 2008, succeeding Hall of Famer Nick Barna as head coach at Damascus Christian. He served in that capacity for 10 seasons before overseeing the transition when DCA closed and became Calkins.

This winter, Jones is excited about the possibility of his team going all the way.

"We finished third overall last year," he said. "We play the second place team this Friday and are in a tournament with last year's champion Dec. 4-5. Those games should give us a good barometer as to where we are."
