articles.title: Jimbo Fisher, Rick Stockstill stir FSU nostalgia. But future may be Glenn Schumann
articles.summary: Jimbo Fisher. Rick Stockstill. Glenn Schumann. Different generations, different visions. FSU must decide who can lead the next one.
articles.body:
Florida State 's coaching search has evolved into a fascinating journey across generations.

For all that has changed in college football, FSU continues to find itself looking to the past as it searches for its future head coach.

There's nothing wrong with that. Some of the program's greatest memories live there, and different generations of Seminoles fans naturally connect with different eras of success. Today's fans want that same feeling, too, especially after experiencing it just three short years ago.

FSU coaching search: 10 possible candidates to replace Mike Norvell

FSU leadership, now including new athletics director Jeff Purinton , has stressed since it fired Mike Norvell Nov. 1 that the search is about upside, adaptability and finding a coach equipped for where college football is going.

Georgia DC Glenn Schumann emerges as top candidate

FSU has expressed a preference for a sitting head coach with a proven track record but remains willing to consider an elite coordinator.

While FSU alum and former graduate assistant Manny Diaz, now the head coach at Duke, and Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann have generated the most steam, Schumann, 36, appears to be emerging as the favorite despite never having been a head coach.

That shouldn't come as a surprise. Schumann has been on the Seminoles' radar from the beginning because of his combination of elite recruiting, championship pedigree and ties to both the region and FSU.

What about Jimbo Fisher or Rick Stockstill as FSU head coach?

Still, one debate among FSU fans refuses to fade: Where should the Seminoles' next head coach come from?

Few names illustrate that better than Rick Stockstill and Jimbo Fisher.

Their connections to FSU stretch across different generations of Seminoles football, resonating with generations of fans who naturally believe in their guy.

Stockstill, 68, former FSU quarterback, connects one generation to the Bobby Bowden years and the foundation of the standard that transformed FSU into a national power.

He also has quickly rejuvenated the fan base with consecutive road wins since being named the Seminoles' interim head coach. FSU (5-5) can become bowl eligible for the first time since 2023 with a homecoming victory over North Carolina State on Saturday at Doak Campbell Stadium.

Stockstill also has something else at stake. He said Monday that he hopes the Seminoles' late-season turnaround leads to another head coaching opportunity, whether at FSU or elsewhere.

Meanwhile, the 61-year-old Fisher, a former assistant under Bowden at FSU, connects another generation to the program's return to that standard. That culminated with the Seminoles' third and most recent national championship in 2013, a season that was considered one of the most dominant of the BCS and modern college football eras.

A loud and passionate segment of fans, former players, boosters and alumni has pushed for Fisher's return on social media, even prior to Norvell's firing as the Seminoles' struggles mounted. A reunion, according to Democrat sources, wasn't going to happen from the start. But that hasn't quieted the campaign. Instead, it has made Fisher one of the most polarizing debates of the coaching search among some FSU faithful.

Different generations. Different memories. Same emotional pull.

Jimbo Fisher or Rick Stockstill? FSU fans across generations must come together

Meet FSU interim coach Rick Stockstill, an FSU Athletics Hall of Famer

Yet it's going to take FSU fans across all generations to pull together and help return football to national prominence when the new coach is introduced.

The previous generation has done its part.

Stockstill's passion for FSU is off the charts. He has quickly reminded the fan base that Seminoles football can be successful and, just as importantly, fun. That's how it felt for most of the Bowden era. Beat the Wolfpack on homecoming, and Stockstill's legend at FSU only grows, along with the gratitude of a fan base that has embraced him, no matter his age.

Fisher offers a different reminder. Despite the bitter ending to his tenure, the ACC football analyst has continued to speak favorably, and at times emotionally, about his years at FSU and what the program meant to a career highlighted by championship success.

Now FSU leadership must figure out who can make it that way again.

That's the dilemma at the heart of this search: Can FSU distinguish between the coach who wins the hiring cycle and the coach who can start winning football games immediately?

Sitting head coach or coordinator, regardless of the price tag, FSU's next hire must be able to sell a vision, energize the fan base and make people believe again.

Because the next coach won't be hired simply to reconnect FSU with its past.

He'll be hired to define its next generation.

Jim Henry is sports editor of the Tallahassee Democrat. Email him at jjhenry@tallahassee.com .

articles.title: When does Ohio State need to trim its playing rotation?
articles.summary: There's little argument that Ohio State isn't deeper than it was a season ago., but five games in the Buckeyes have to start trimming their rotation.
articles.body:
Ohio State men's basketball coach Jake Diebler would prefer this to the problem he faced a year ago.

When the Buckeyes fought their way into the 2026 NCAA Tournament, they didn't have much of a bench to lean on. Ohio State ranked 327th nationally in percentage of minutes played from its reserves, according to KenPom.com, and that lack of depth ultimately proved critical in Diebler's second season.

This year's course correction involved bringing in nine new players, most of whom are reasonably expected to contribute at some meaningful level in 2026-27. But at halftime of a Nov. 16 home game against Prairie View A&M , Diebler got his latest reminder that sometimes you can have too much of a good thing.

Eleven different Buckeyes were on the floor for at least 3:25 of the first half as OSU eked out a 34-29 lead. Diebler shortened his rotation in the second half, and the Buckeyes went on to a comfortable 86-59 win . Afterward, Diebler pointed out how many guys had seen first-half minutes and noted that the coaches were still figuring that out.

Photos from Ohio States 86-59 victory over Prairie View A&M

He was asked if an 11-man rotation is feasible for an entire season.

A Nov. 19 home game with UMBC is OSU's last tune-up before another high-major showdown – a Nov. 24 home game against No. 15 Vanderbilt. Ohio State has just four more games against mid-major teams on the schedule, including UMBC.

It's time for Diebler to start trimming the rotation.

"It's hard," he said. "There were many times last year where I would've begged to deal with this problem. I still believe this is a good problem to have. We're evaluating everything, including practice significantly for some guys, to help decide the back end of our rotation."

The second half against Prairie View A&M was a glimpse into the process. Of the 11 players to see first-half action, three did not step onto the court until the second half was past its midway point and the Ohio State lead was at least 19 points.

In addition to seeing who's performing well on any given game day, Diebler is also using practices to help him divvy up minutes.

Case in point: late-summer acquisition Lee Aaliya . The veteran forward has multiple years of international experience, but his preseason was truncated by an illness just as Diebler said he was starting to hit his stride. The staff still believes that Aaliya will be a significant contributor this season, but he has had just 17:15 of playing time in four appearances to show that.

"Right now we need to put more emphasis on what he's doing in practice versus the limited opportunity he's having in the game," Diebler said. "That's the most reasonable way to approach it. Now, he needs to practice consistently because he's getting opportunity to play way more in practice."

Last season, Ohio State had three games in which at least 10 different players scored at least one point. This year, that has happened in three of the first five games. It's clear there are more capable players on this year's roster than at any point in Diebler's first two full seasons on the job.

For this team to get where it wants to be by season's end, the playing time is going to start to dwindle for the players at the back end of the rotation. Those are the decisions Diebler and his staff will have to make.

And asked when that needs to start happening, Diebler didn't hesitate.

"Now," he said. "I think we have to start being even more specific. We don't have this runway of games. Every game for us is important. If you drag this out too long, you can almost stunt the growth of the team. That's the fine line we're thinking through of how we're processing that."

articles.title: 2 elite Texas A&M 2027 commits are now 5-star prospects
articles.summary: Texas A&M 2027 commits, safety Kamarui Dorsey and DL Myles Smith are now 5-star commits in the latest 247Sports rankings.
articles.body:
Texas A&M's No. 2-ranked 2027 recruiting class has become the primary focus for coach Mike Elko and his staff, especially after five-star offensive tackle Mark Matthews flipped his commitment to Georgia and four-star linebacker Aston Whiteside flipped to Miami.

With four-star wide receiver Jaden Upshaw set to visit Alabama during next Saturday's Iron Bowl matchup vs. Auburn, pressure is mounting on Mike Elko, especially given Upshaw's close relationship with first-year offensive coordinator Holmon Wiggins, who has led his recruitment.

If Holmon Wiggins isn't retained after the 2026 season, Upshaw is certainly a candidate to flip his commitment, but based on recent interviews, the Georgia native remains "100% committed" until further notice. On Wednesday, two of the Aggies' blue-chip 2027 commits , safety Kamarui Dorsey and defensive lineman Myels Smith, steadily rose in the latest 247Sports rankings.

Both players have shut down their recruitments and are considered first-year contributors with extremely bright futures; as of Monday, they are now five-star prospects, even though Kamarui Dorsey moved down to No. 16 while Myels Smith shot up from 39th to 18th overall.

Despite Texas A&M's immense struggles this season, Kamarui Dorsey and four-star DB JayQuan Snell are considered the next starting safety duo, while Myels Smith is widely considered the most dominant defensive tackle in the 2027 cycle.

articles.title: Lions CB D.J. Reed: 'I don't want to rush' return from hip injury
articles.summary: D.J. Reed is expected to miss his third straight game this week with a hip injury he suffered against the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
In hindsight, D.J. Reed probably came back too early from the hamstring strain he suffered last season. And now that he's over the initial frustration of having to miss more time with a hip injury, the Detroit Lions' No. 1 cornerback is being careful not to make that mistake again.

"I definitely want to make sure I come back and I feel like myself," Reed said Wednesday, Nov. 18. "I don't want to rush it especially cause our defense is playing well so I don't want to be a hindrance. So I just got to be honest with myself and be honest with the trainers and my coaches to see if I'm ready to go, whenever that is."

Reed has not played since injuring his hip on a key fourth-and-5 pass breakup in the fourth quarter of the Lions ' Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings . He said he likely will miss his third straight game Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Last year, Reed was playing good football when he hurt his hamstring in a September game against the Cleveland Browns. He was diagnosed with a Grade II/ III strain , missed six weeks, then struggled upon his return.

That experience has colored Reed's conservative approach to his current rehab. He said he doesn't expect to spend time on injured reserve, but called his return date "up in the air."

"When you get hurt you obviously want to get back on the field as soon as possible," Reed said. "But I kind of [underestimated] the severity of a hamstring strain, especially a high-grade one, cause I never hurt my hamstring that bad. So in hindsight, yes, I do feel like I came back early. So dealing with this right here, I just definitely want to make sure I definitely come back confident, healthy and ready to play compared to coming back and not being myself. That's not smart, that's not helping the team."

The Lions (7-2) have won five straight and have gotten improved play from their secondary in recent weeks.

Roger McCreary and Rock Ya-Sin played most of the game at corner in last week's win over the New England Patriots. Khalil Dorsey, Ennis Rakestraw Jr. and Nick Whiteside also are in the rotation at cornerback. And All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph is expected to make his long-awaited return from a knee injury Sunday.

Reed, who got off to a rocky start to this season, allowed just six catches for 41 yards on 14 pass targets in the three games before he got hurt.

He said he needs to regain his burst and top-end speed in training before he's ready to return to action.

"Everything's in the air right now so we're just trying to hit top-end speeds, trying to make sure that I can run and make sure that I can cover and stay in front of people without it hurting, without it pulling," he said. "Kind of just going day-by-day, so it's kind of in the air."

articles.title: Nebraska continues dominating start with big win over Mount St. Mary's
articles.summary: Nebraska returned home to take on Mount St. Mary's. The Huskers continued their dominating start to the season, blowing out the Mountaineers 113-37.
articles.body:
Nebraska women's basketball (5-0) returned home to take on Mount St. Mary's (0-6) for a Tuesday night showdown. The Huskers continued their dominating start to the season, blowing out the Mountaineers 113-37.

This win marks Nebraska's second-straight 100-point game and sets a school record for the largest margin of victory (76) against an NCAA Division I opponent. This was also the Huskers' fourth-highest scoring total in program history.

Nebraska dominated from the start, finishing the night hitting 40-of-66 from the floor, 9-of-22 from beyond the arc and 24-of-27 from the free-throw line. The Huskers also held Mount St. Mary's to 13-of-61, 1-of-23 and 10-of-12, respectively. Nebraska dominated on the boards as well, outrebounding the Mountaineers 51-18.

Natalie Potts led the Huskers with a double-double, scoring a game-high 18 points and securing a game-high 10 rebounds. Potts shot 5-of-8, 1-of-2 and 7-of-8, respectively. Amiah Hargrove and Britt Prince finished behind Potts in scoring, both finishing with 16 points. Prince finished 6-of-7 from the floor and 4-of-4 from the line. Hargrove hit 5-of-7, 2-of-3 and 4-of-4, respectively.

Logan Nissley scored 13 points, which included a game-high 3-of-6 from beyond the arc. Freshman Ava Miles totaled 11 points, going 4-of-6 from the floor and 2-of-2 from the free-throw line. Indiana Edessa Noyan and Emily Fisher both scored 10 points.

Nebraska travels up I-80 for its next matchup. The Huskers clash with in-state rival Creighton on Sunday at Liberty First Credit Union in Ralston, Nebraska. Tip-off is set for 1 p.m. CT on FS1.
